metaDescription: Table lamps under $100 compared on height, shade, dimming, USB ports and wireless charging, with honest notes on bedside versus living room scale and shade fit.
expertTake: The Seaside village 25 inch lamp is the best overall pick because it states stepless dimming, USB-C and USB-A ports and a stable metal base at a living room height. The Adesso two-light lamp is the best value for a bright, classic lamp with two pull chains. Skip bedside-scale lamps for a sofa side table, because a 15 inch lamp looks small beside a sofa arm.
introParagraphs: A table lamp is the easiest layer of light in a living room: it sits on a side table or console, plugs into the wall and gives a warm pool of light that a ceiling fixture cannot. The detail that decides whether a lamp works is scale, since a lamp that suits a nightstand looks tiny beside a sofa.

The cap reflects listing prices on the day we updated the guide, and prices move often. We favoured lamps with a stated height, a shade and a control scheme, and kept the lineup distinct from our under 50 guide with two carry-overs. We have not handled any of these lamps, so our judgments rest on specifications and patterns in owner feedback, including touch sensors, charging ports and shade wobble.

products.name: Seaside village 25 Inch Table Lamp with USB-C and USB-A Ports, stepless dimming, metal base, drum shade

specList.label: Ports
specList.value: USB-C and USB-A on the side

products.description:
This lamp stands 25 inches tall, a living room scale rather than a nightstand scale, with USB-C and USB-A ports built into the side, a fully stepless rotary dimmer and a sturdy metal base and pole under a hardback drum shade. A 25 inch lamp sits comfortably beside a sofa or on a console. The USB ports charge phones without a separate brick.

The tradeoff is that built-in ports add electronics to a lamp and the charging output is modest, and the compact data gives no lumens. Compared with the PoKat, the Seaside village is taller and simpler in style. Metal poles are stable, but a slim base can still be bumped.

Place it on a stable table with the cord hidden behind. Use a warm LED bulb of 2700K. Do not overload the USB ports.
products.bestFor: A side table beside a sofa that needs a lamp with charging and smooth dimming.
pros: 25 inch height suits a sofa side table
USB-C and USB-A ports built in
cons: Built-in ports add electronics that can fail

products.name: Adesso Boulevard 2-Light Table Lamp, brushed steel, white fabric shade, 28 inch, dual pull chains
products.description:
This is a classic two-light table lamp 28 inches tall with a brushed steel base, a white fabric shade, dual pull chains and a 60 inch cord. Two sockets let you run one or both bulbs for a wider range of light, and a 100 watt rating leaves room for bright bulbs. It is the tallest lamp in the group and the most traditional.

The compromise is that a pull chain is old-school, and the compact data gives no dimmer or smart option. Compared with the Seaside village, it gives more light but fewer features. A two-light lamp is a good reading lamp and a bright ambient lamp.

Use LED bulbs to stay within the rating and keep heat down. Check the shade is seated properly on the harp. Place it on a stable table.
products.bestFor: A traditional living room that wants a bright, reliable lamp with two sockets.
pros: Two lights let you choose one or both
28 inch height suits a living room
Brushed steel base is easy to wipe
cons: Pull chains are less convenient than touch or dimmers

products.name: Seealle 16.1 Inch Touch Table Lamp, 3-way dimmable, bulb included, black
products.description:
This is a 16.1 inch nightstand lamp with touch control anywhere on the body, three brightness levels and a bulb included. The listing says you can read on the high setting and relax on a lower one. Touch lamps avoid fiddling for a switch in the dark.

The tradeoff is scale and control: 16 inches is small for a living room, and touch sensors can misfire with static or a nearby hand. Compared with the Seaside village, it is smaller and simpler, with coarser dimming. Bulb included saves a purchase.

Place it on a nightstand or a small side table. Keep the cord tidy. Touch the lamp gently and do not tap repeatedly.
products.bestFor: A bedside or a small side table where touch control is handy.
cons: Small scale for a living room

products.name: iGaur Nightstand Lamp with Wireless Charger, 4-in-1 touch lamp with Bluetooth speaker, dimmable LED
products.description:
This lamp packs four features into one: a touch dimmable LED lamp with four brightness levels, a wireless phone charging pad, a Bluetooth 5.0 speaker with a 33 foot range and a night light function. It suits a bedside table where you want a charger and music in one spot. The speaker is a simple 2.0 system.

The compromise is that a multi-function lamp is a compromise lamp: the speaker will not match a real speaker, and a wireless charger is slow compared with a cable. Compared with the Seaside village, it adds a speaker and a wireless pad but less light. More electronics means more things that can fail.

Check that your phone case allows wireless charging. Place the phone centred on the pad. Keep the lamp away from water.
products.bestFor: A bedside or desk where a lamp, a charger and a speaker share a footprint.
pros: Wireless charging pad is built in

products.name: PoKat 20.75 Inch Small Modern Ceramic Table Lamps Set of 2, white, farmhouse, for nightstands
products.description:
This is a matched pair of 20.75 inch white ceramic table lamps with shades that you install yourself, to save on packaging. A pair flanks a bed or a sofa and gives a symmetrical look. Ceramic bases are heavy and stable, which suits a lamp that sits on a console.

The tradeoff is that ceramic can chip or crack if knocked, and the compact data does not mention a dimmer or a bulb. Compared with the Seaside village, you get two lamps and a softer look but fewer features. This pair also appears in our under 50 guide.

Assemble the shade carefully and check it sits straight. Use a warm LED bulb. Place the pair a few feet apart.
products.bestFor: A symmetrical pair for a sofa console, a mantel or a bed.
pros: 20.75 inch height suits a nightstand or console
White farmhouse look suits many rooms
cons: Shades need installation and no dimmer is listed

products.name: GOEBLESON Tripod Table Lamp, 14.6 Inch, beige linen shade, solid wood tripod
products.description:
This small lamp is 14.6 inches tall with a wood tripod base and a beige linen shade described as high density, in a mid-century modern style. The linen diffuses light softly, and the tripod gives a stable stance with a light look. It is a nightstand lamp and a small desk lamp.

The compromise is size: at 14.6 inches it is too small for most living room side tables. Compared with the Seaside village, it is smaller, warmer and plainer. It also appears in our under 50 guide.

Place it on a nightstand or a small shelf. Use a warm LED bulb. Check the tripod screws.
products.bestFor: A nightstand or small desk where a soft linen shade fits.
pros: High-density linen shade diffuses light softly
cons: Too small for a living room side table
Also appears in our under 50 guide

buyingCriteria.explanation: At this cap a table lamp adds a living room height, a stepless dimmer, built-in ports or a matched pair. The Seaside village states ports and stepless dimming, and the Adesso states a two-light design. Our under 50 guide covers simpler lamps. Measure the surface the lamp will sit on, since a lamp with a wide shade needs a table at least as wide as the shade and some margin for a drink or a book. Look at the lamp from the sofa before deciding on height, since the bottom of the shade should sit at about eye level when seated to avoid glare.

A lamp on a side table beside a sofa should be about 24 to 30 inches tall, so the shade bottom sits near eye level when you are seated. A 15 inch lamp is for a nightstand. A lamp that is too small looks lost. Look at the cord length and where the switch sits: a cord on the wrong side forces an ugly route across the room, and an inline switch is easier to reach than a socket switch on a tall lamp.

A fabric or linen shade diffuses light and cuts glare, and a hardback drum shade gives a clean look. A shade should be about as wide as the base is tall at its widest. Warm 2700K bulbs suit living rooms. If the lamp will sit near a sofa arm, check that the shade is high enough that you do not bump it when you sit down, and that the base is not too wide for the table.

A stepless dimmer is smooth, three-way switches are coarse, and touch controls can misfire. Pull chains are reliable but old-fashioned. Make sure the bulb is dimmable for any dimmer. Think about colour and finish in relation to the room: a metal base reads cooler, a ceramic base warmer, and a wood base the warmest of the three.

Built-in USB ports save a plug and keep a console tidy. Wireless pads are convenient but slow and depend on your phone case. Electronics in a lamp add failure points. Decide whether you want a lamp as a pair or a single, because a pair on either side of a sofa makes the room look balanced and a single suits an asymmetrical corner.

A heavy ceramic or metal base resists tipping, and a light base can be knocked over. Tripods look light but are stable on a flat surface. Keep cords tidy. Check whether the bulb is included and what type it is, because a fixed LED module cannot be replaced and a standard socket lets you swap in a warmer or brighter bulb.

specDecoder.meaning: The overall height of the lamp including the shade. Measure from the table surface to the top of the shade, not to the top of the base, so the lamp's real height fits the space.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Adesso is 28 inches, Seaside village 25, PoKat 20.75, Seealle 16.1 and GOEBLESON 14.6.

specDecoder.meaning: Dimming that slides smoothly without fixed levels. A rotary dimmer feels smooth because it varies the current continuously, while a touch lamp steps through preset levels.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Seaside village lists fully stepless dimming.

specDecoder.meaning: A lamp with three fixed brightness levels. Touch lamps cycle through off, low, medium and high, so a wrong tap means cycling again.
A pad that charges a compatible phone without a cable. A wireless charging pad only works with a compatible phone and a thin case, and it runs slower than a cable.
specDecoder.watchFor: The iGaur lists a wireless pad.

specDecoder.meaning: The wire frame that holds the shade over the bulb. The harp is the wire loop that holds the shade, and a bent harp is a common reason a shade sits crooked.
specDecoder.watchFor: The PoKat requires the shade to be installed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Scale and height
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each lamp on the height stated in its listing. The Adesso and Seaside village suit a living room, and the rest suit a bedside. We have not handled any of these lamps. We looked at how each lamp is controlled, since a switch you cannot find in the dark is the commonest complaint about bedside lamps. We treated every listing without a stated height as unknown and did not guess.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dimmers, ports and chargers. Owner feedback patterns often mention touch sensors that misfire and ports that fail. We compared heights against typical living room side tables, which is why the shorter lamps are labelled as bedside choices.

howWeEvaluated.title: Shade and light
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered shade materials and the light they give. We do not publish ratings or review counts. We read each listing for bulb details, since a lamp sold without a bulb may need a separate purchase and a lamp with a fixed module cannot be repaired.

howWeEvaluated.title: Distinct from our under 50 guide
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept the lineup distinct from our under 50 guide, with two carry-overs. We separated lamps built for a living room from lamps built for a nightstand, because the best lamp for one is not the best for the other.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: Listings often omit lumens and bulb details. Where a number is missing, we say so.

cards.label: Touch or rotary dimmer
cards.text: Smooth control in the dark. Touch sensors can misfire.

cards.label: Pull chain
cards.text: Simple and reliable. Needs reaching and gives no dimming.

howToChoose.note: Choose a dimmer for a living room and a pull chain for a simple reading lamp.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A height of 24 to 30 inches, a warm dimmable bulb and a stable base.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Seaside village and Adesso are the best fit for a living room.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a designer base, a hand-finished shade or a lamp with a smart bulb included.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a simple lamp for a bedside. A basic lamp is enough.

maintenance.why: Dust dims light and shows. Wipe the base with a damp cloth and dry it, and use a dry cloth on the shade to avoid water marks. Keep the cord out of walkways and tidy it with clips so it does not get caught.
A loose socket flickers. Replace a flickering bulb before blaming the lamp, since a worn LED is the commonest cause.
Cords fray at the base. Check that the shade sits level and that the harp is tight, which also keeps the bulb clear of the fabric.
Dust blocks connectors. Clear dust from USB ports and charging pads with a dry brush and keep drinks away from them.
A wobbling base is a tip risk.

faq.q: How tall should a table lamp be?
faq.a: About 24 to 30 inches for a sofa side table, and about 15 to 20 for a nightstand. Choose a warm white bulb of 2700K for the living room, because cool bulbs make a lamp feel like an office light. Place the lamp where the shade will not touch curtains or a wall.
A warm 2700K LED. Use a dimmable bulb for a dimmer. If a lamp seems too dim, check the bulb wattage rating on the socket and use a brighter LED within that limit.

faq.q: Do USB ports in a lamp work well?
faq.a: For phones, yes, though output is modest. Keep fabric shades about an inch from a hot bulb, and use LED bulbs to avoid heat marks.
They work, but sensors can misfire. A lamp on a console behind a sofa needs a taller base so the shade sits above the sofa back.
Yes. The cap reflects listing prices when we updated the guide, and prices move often. If the lamp wobbles, check that the base is flat and that the table surface is level.

faq.q: How wide should the shade be?
faq.a: Roughly as wide as the base is at its widest. Consider a smart plug if you want the lamp to turn on at a set time without changing the lamp's controls.
